{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has a concrete payer (creators) and a price anchored to published pricing: Memberful at $49/mo + 4.9%, against Patreon's 10% + processing. Idea B's own brief says the concept is unconfirmed ('one-line description to confirm') and the customer 'varies by idea'.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence is two sourced r/patreon posts about fees from creators who already pay and are looking to switch. Idea B's only demand evidence is one post seen through a mirror site, and the same thread contains a direct rebuttal of the premise ('you can just vibe code if you have an idea').",
    "Idea A's competitors show the market pays: Patreon, Memberful and Fourthwall all publish fee structures, and Ko-fi claims 1M creators. Idea B's direct competitors are free, pre-revenue, or showing labelled dummy data. Only the adjacent CoFoundersLab shows paid conversion.",
    "Idea A has a sourced precedent for its wedge: a niche-focused membership platform that reached about $140K MRR and an exit. It also names a concrete path to a first customer, which is direct outreach to a niche community. Idea B has no comparable success case.",
    "Idea A has serious risks: a saturated SERP, incumbents at 0% fees, and real compliance load. These are execution risks in a market with proven willingness to pay. Idea B's risks are about whether a need and a payer exist at all, which matters more under a 90-day paying-customer goal."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence is a single Reddit post accessed through a third-party mirror. That thread contains a direct counterargument that AI vibe-coding removes the need. It does not show anyone willing to pay. The supporting acquisition-cost figure ($100–200 per paying customer) comes from a vendor blog the brief itself marks as not independently verified.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderately high confidence that A is the better first bet, mainly because B is under-specified and lacks a payer. A is still a weak bet in absolute terms. Its only success precedent depended on the founder having an owned niche audience. Its CAC is unknown given incumbent SEO dominance. Its payments compliance (KYC/money-transmitter, 1099-K, sales tax) could slow a solo operator's path to a first paying customer within 90 days."
}
